---
title: Capture and recording
description: Photos, stills, screenshots and video out of the same session that is already drawing.
---

Capture runs on the live session, so what somebody saves is what they were
looking at, lens and overlays and all.

## A photo

```c
goss_engine_capture_photo(engine, ...);
goss_engine_capture_photo_as(engine, ...);   /* with a format and quality */
```

Reach for `capture_photo_as` when wherever it's going has an opinion about
format, quality, colour space or bit depth.

## A still at a size you choose

A still is a photo rendered at whatever resolution you ask for, which is how
you get an image bigger than the preview without running the preview itself at
that size.

```c
goss_engine_capture_still(engine, &config, ...);
```

The config carries width, height, supersampling, format, quality, colour space
and bit depth. Supersampling is what decides whether the result looks like a
screenshot or like a photo.

## The current frame

```c
goss_engine_capture_frame(engine, ...);
goss_engine_capture_live_frame(engine, ...);
```

`capture_frame` gives you the composed frame. `capture_live_frame` gives you
what's on screen right now, which is what a "save this moment" button wants.

## A screenshot of what is drawn

```c
goss_engine_request_screenshot(engine, ...);
```

The request gets queued and answered on a later frame instead of blocking the
one in flight, so watch for it in the event drain rather than waiting.

## Video

```c
goss_engine_recording_start(engine, ...);
goss_engine_recording_pause(engine);
goss_engine_recording_resume(engine);
goss_engine_recording_stop(engine, ...);
```

Recording has a real-time mode:

```c
goss_engine_recording_set_realtime(engine, true);
```

Real-time keeps the recording in step with the clock and drops work rather than
falling behind. Turn it off and it prefers completeness over timing, which is
what an export wants and not what a live capture does.

Read the report instead of guessing how it's going:

```c
goss_engine_recording_read_report(engine, &report);
```

That report tells you whether the recording is healthy, and it's what belongs
in a developer build rather than a spinner.

## Sealing media

```c
goss_seal_media(...);
```

Sealing marks media as having come from this engine. Use it if provenance
matters to what you're building.

## Practical notes

- Capture competes with the preview for the same budget. A still at four times
  the preview resolution isn't free, and the ladder will notice.
- Ask for the format you actually want. Converting afterwards costs more than
  asking up front.
- Recording holds buffers, so stop it when the user leaves the screen rather
  than when the session ends.
